note: After the decisive Jagiellonian victory at Grunwald (1410), the Teutonic Order's military power was permanently broken. The subsequent Thirteen Years' War (1454–1466) — fought with Polish-Lithuanian support for the Prussian Confederation of cities that revolted against the Order — ended with the Second Peace of Thorn (1466): the Order ceded Royal Prussia to Poland (including Danzig/Gdańsk and the Vistula corridor) and became a Polish vassal for the remaining Ducal Prussia. The Order's last Prussian grand master, Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach, converted to Lutheranism (1525) and secularized the remaining territory as the Duchy of Prussia.

_quarry.structural_significance: Grunwald permanently ends the Teutonic Order's military expansion; the Second Peace of Thorn gives Poland Baltic access and riverine dominance; Albert's secularization of Ducal Prussia (1525) creates the nucleus of the future Prussian state that eventually absorbs Poland
